newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tadiran Appliance gets foreign partner.
newsitem.headline: Tadiran Appliance gets foreign partner.

text.p: Israel's Tadiran Electrical Appliances Ltd hopes to build its air conditioning business with the help of an unnamed foreign company that has agreed to take a 26 percent stake in it, a Tadiran executive said on Thursday.

Shlomo Zohar, Tadiran Appliance's chief financial officer, told Reuters that the foreign firm would be providing the company with technical know-how, production support and assistance in marketing and distribution overseas.
Tadiran Ltd, which holds 88 percent of Tadiran Appliances, said on Wednesday that the foreign company had agreed to acquire a 26 percent of Tadiran Appliances subject to due diligence.

It said the price would be equivalent to Tadiran Appliances' equity, which was $64 million at the end of the third quarter, plus a 10 percent premium. That would make the sale price about $18 million.

Tadiran said the buyer would have a three-year option to buy further shares. Zohar would not provide any further details about the options nor comment on newspaper reports that the foreign company was seeking control of Tadiran Appliance.
Zohar said he expected the sale to be completed at the start of next year.

Air conditioners are an important part of Tadiran Appliances' revenues, which were 470 million shekels in the first nine months of 1996, but Zohar would not say what portion of the total. The company also makes refrigerators and other home appliances.
Exports, mainly to Europe, make up about 20 percent of total sales, Zohar said.
